profile.reading: Pearl Plaza Office Building sits at 601 East 18th Avenue in the North Capitol Hill neighborhood of Denver, Colorado, immediately east of the state capitol. Public address records identify the occupant of the building as the Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT), the state agency that runs shared computing and network infrastructure for Colorado state government. The building is a modest three story commercial office structure, not a purpose built or converted data center. It appears in this registry because an OpenStreetMap contributor tagged it with a CLLI code, a type of location identifier the telecommunications industry assigns to central offices and other facilities that carry telecom equipment, together with a general data center tag. That combination most plausibly reflects a telecom equipment room or network point of presence serving the tenants of the building and the state IT operations housed there, rather than a wholesale or retail colocation facility open to outside customers. No square footage, power capacity, or other data center specification is published for this address, because none applies to what public records indicate is a government office building rather than a dedicated data center.

reading.body:
Pearl Plaza Office Building is a state government office building at 601 East 18th Avenue in Denver, not a commercial data center. The published specifications identify it as the home of the Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology, the agency that runs shared IT infrastructure for Colorado state government. No power capacity, square footage, or other data center specification is published for this address because the building is a government office, not a dedicated facility for wholesale or retail colocation.

The OpenStreetMap tagging that placed this building in the registry reflects a CLLI code, a telecommunications industry location identifier that most plausibly marks a telecom equipment room or network point of presence serving the building's tenants and state IT operations, rather than a data center facility open to outside customers. No published specifications exist to convert into capacity estimates for AI workloads.

This facility does not meaningfully rank among Colorado's mapped data center assets for AI scaling purposes. The state has 17 mapped facilities, of which only 3 publish power specifications totaling 26.35 MW. This building is not among those three published capacity sites and should be excluded from analyses of grid constraints on AI infrastructure in Colorado.
